result:
Everything looks clean and scoped to the task. Final summary:

I implemented the welcome-email feature as a background job so registration never waits on mail delivery:

- **`config/queue.ts`** / **`config/mail.ts`** — new config modules building a `QueueManager` (drivers `sync`/`memory`/`redis`, selected by `QUEUE_CONNECTION`) and a `MailManager` (transports `log`/`resend`, selected by `MAIL_MAILER`, with `from` sourced from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME`), mirroring the existing `config/database.ts` pattern.
- **`app/Providers/QueueServiceProvider.ts`** / **`app/Providers/MailServiceProvider.ts`** — new providers (scaffolded via `bunx guren make:provider`) that bind these managers into the container and, on `boot()`, call the framework's global `setQueueDriver()`/`setMailManager()`/`registerJob()` — wired into `src/app.ts`'s `providers` list.
- **`app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`** — a `Mail` subclass (via `bunx guren make:mail`) building the `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!` subject and a plain-text greeting.
- **`app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts`** — a `Job` subclass (via `bunx guren make:job`) whose `handle()` reads the *current* global mail manager (`getMailManager()`) at run time and sends `WelcomeMail`, so a worker/test can swap the mailer after dispatch.
- **`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts`** — after creating and logging in the user, dispatches `SendWelcomeEmailJob.dispatch({ name, email })`; this only runs past validation/duplicate-email checks, so refused registrations queue nothing.
- **`tests/RegisterController.test.ts`** — new test using `@guren/testing`'s `fakeQueue()`/`fakeMail()` to verify registration pushes exactly one job and sends no mail inline, that manually running the job sends exactly one correctly-addressed/subject-lined email, and that a refused registration queues and sends nothing.

`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (4 tests, including the 2 pre-existing ones) both pass, and `bunx guren check` reports no failures.
